description: We are Arthur and Antoine, two French high school seniors based in Singapore. We are participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge to test ourselves and build hands-on experience.
summary: Space Sweeper is an interactive resource-management game developed to raise awareness about the growing, critical threat of orbital debris. Addressing the challenge of simulating a complete space mission, our game puts players in charge of a vital clean-up operation in Earth's orbit. Players alternate between a planning phase—making engineering trade-offs to upgrade energy production, fuel capacity, and magnet power using limited budgets—and an active mission phase where they navigate a spacecraft to collect debris before their fuel runs out. By balancing these competing demands, players experience the complex realities of mission design. Ultimately, Space Sweeper makes the abstract problem of space pollution tangible, educating players on why keeping our orbit clean is essential for the safety of astronauts, satellites, and future space exploration.
details:
What it does and how it works: Space Sweeper is an educational simulation game divided into two core phases. In the Plan Phase, players manage a limited budget to make critical engineering decisions, upgrading their spacecraft's energy production, fuel capacity, and magnet power. In the Game Phase, players actively pilot the spacecraft through Earth's orbit, using their upgraded magnet to collect space debris. Once the spacecraft's fuel runs out, the mission ends, and players earn funds based on the debris collected to reinvest in the next planning phase. This continuous loop simulates the iterative nature of space mission design.

Intended impact and benefits: Space is becoming increasingly crowded, with over 50,000 large objects threatening satellites and future missions. Our goal is to sensitize the public to this danger. By transforming a complex issue into an interactive gaming experience, we make the problem of space pollution accessible. The game also provides a hands-on understanding of the competing demands in aerospace engineering, as players must constantly balance mass, power, and budget constraints to succeed.

Tools, coding languages, and software used: As two high school seniors looking to build hands-on experience, we developed this game using the Unity game engine. The core logic and gameplay mechanics were scripted in C#. We also utilized 3D modeling tools to adapt real NASA assets for our game environment, and leveraged AI tools to help us learn the Unity platform and troubleshoot code.

Creativity and factors considered: To make the abstract concepts of orbital constraints and mission trade-offs engaging, we gamified the experience into a satisfying loop. We creatively repurposed the NASA Gamma-Ray Observatory 3D model, modifying it into our specialized "magnet satellite." We also integrated a real NASA satellite launch video as a cinematic cutscene to immerse players in the mission from the very beginning.
